name: Four-barrel all-metal-sealed pipe-gun D2 pellet injector for the ST40 spherical tokamak cooled to ~8 K by a Sumitomo RDK-415 GM cryocooler in a guard vacuum chamber
plain_name: Make millimetre-size frozen deuterium pellets inside a vacuum box chilled by a closed-cycle cooler, to refuel a compact spherical tokamak
description: ORNL-Tokamak Energy design (from proven pellet-injector-in-a-suitcase and JET/KSTAR SPI hardware): 1.2-2.0 mm D2 cylinders frozen in barrels at ~8 K by a GM cryocooler inside a guard vacuum chamber pumped to ~1e-2 mbar, fired at 200-500 m/s.
keywords: Make millimetre-size frozen deuterium pellets inside a vacuum box chilled by a closed-cycle cooler, to refuel a compact spherical tokamak

sources.citation: Baylor & Wilson, Conceptual Design of a Pellet Injector for the ST40, ORNL/Tokamak Energy INFUSE report (2022)

reported_equipment: ORNL pellet injector in a suitcase
guard vacuum chamber with 10-inch conflat flanges

requirements.rationale: Barrel cold zones must reach ~8 K.
Guard vacuum chamber provides thermal insulation.
Guard vacuum must reach ~1e-2 mbar for the cryocooler.
Electrical feedthrough flanges on the chamber.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
